title: Cap. V Obj. 8 Sol close: faith and perseverance flow from election — Cap. V Arminian objections end
pass_a_gloss: Nay from the revealed word of God it is rightly deduced that both faith and perseverance in faith depend upon a preceding election or ordination unto life. Hither look those places, Acts 13:48. As many as were ordained to eternal life believed. Matt. 24:24. Seducers would draw even the elect into apostasy, if it were possible. That therefore certain ones believe, and that believers do not spring back from faith, that flows from antecedent election: not, as Arminius wills, that because they are indeed foreseen as about to believe and about to persevere in faith, from thence their election before others flows. We will not heap up more objections from the writings of Arminius, because these being scattered, it is easy also to dissolve all the rest, which are of the same flour. We will therefore at length come to setting forth our defense, and strengthening it with arguments.
pass_b_english: Indeed from God's revealed word it is rightly deduced that both faith and perseverance in faith depend on a preceding election or ordination unto life. So Acts 13:48 — as many as were ordained to eternal life believed — and Matt. 24:24 — seducers would draw even the elect into apostasy if it were possible. That some believe, and that believers do not spring back from faith, flows from antecedent election — not, as Arminius wills, that foresight of their believing and persevering is what makes their election flow before others. We will not heap more objections from Arminius's writings; these scattered, the rest of the same flour are easy to dissolve. We come at last to set out our defense and strengthen it with arguments.
source_text: Imo ex revelato Dei verbo recte deducitur, tum fidem, tum in fide perseverantiam ex praeeunte electione sive ad vitam ordinatione dependere. Huc spectant illa, Actor. xiii. 48. Crediderunt, quotquot ordinati erant ad vitam aeternam. Matth. xxiv. 24. Seductores in apostasiam pertraherent, si possibile esset, ipsos electos. Quod igitur quidam credunt, et quod credentes a fide non resiliunt, id ex antecedente electione dimanat: non, ut vult Arminius, quod quidem praevidentur credituri et in fide perseveraturi, exinde eorundem prae aliis electio dimanat. Plures ex Arminii scriptis objectiones non congeremus, quia hisce dissipatis, facile est et reliquas omnes, quae ejusdem farinae sunt, dissolvere. Veniemus igitur tandem ad defensionem nostram exponendam, et argumentis roborandam.
